overview: Cudahy's despatch finds no 'Central Japanese News Bureau for Europe' in Poland, suggesting observers mistook the small RIENT agency, run by émigré Dzhabagiev, for one; notes Warsaw's Japanese military attaché evaluated intelligence from Poland and the Baltics.

people.name: John Cudahy
people.role: U.S. diplomatic representative in Poland and author of despatch No. 323

people.name: Vassan-Girey Dzhabagiev
people.role: Caucasus-born operator of the RIENT news agency

subfiles.title: Cross-reference for Cudahy despatch No. 323
subfiles.from: Department of State filing staff; referenced source: Cudahy in Poland
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects researchers to file 860c.912/3 for Cudahy’s report on the alleged Central Japanese News Bureau for Europe in Warsaw.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Cudahy's 1934 despatch No. 323 finding the purported Central Japanese News Bureau for Europe apparently did not exist.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 323 on the alleged Japanese news bureau in Warsaw
subfiles.about: Cudahy reports the results of an investigation into an alleged Central Japanese News Bureau for Europe and describes the possibly confused RIENT agency.
subfiles.summary: Cudahy's investigation found no Japanese news bureau in Poland; observers likely mistook RIENT, an émigré agency housed near the Japanese Legation distributing anti-Soviet news, for one, and notes Warsaw's Japanese military attaché evaluated Poland/Baltic intelligence.

interest: Shows a Warsaw news-bureau rumor traced to a small pro-Japanese émigré agency tied to Japan's intelligence network.
